_comment: 🧩️ This subset's own contribution. `s.demonstrator.playground` is a semio-NATIVE artifact carried in `.dsl.semio`/`.pack.semio`, so no third party can serve as its reference — see the noOracleDecision below. Its vocabulary is exactly one kind because its snapshot is exactly one field, and that is a property of the artifact, not an omission.

noOracleDecisions.rationale: No third-party crate reads or writes semio's `.dsl.semio`/`.pack.semio` envelope, and none could be authoritative over `PlaygroundMutation` — a one-variant vocabulary whose single kind retags the artifact's only persistent field. What genuinely distinguishes this subset from every other mutation vocabulary in the repository is that `PlaygroundSnapshot` carries NO `#[serde(tag = ..)]` and its payload struct carries no `rename_all`, so the mutation encodes EXTERNALLY tagged as `{"ChangeSchema": {"new_schema": ..}}` with a snake_case field — the opposite convention from every sibling artifact. Confidence therefore comes from the committed specification vector under `../🧬️schema/🧬️mutations/✒️change-schema/🧪️tests/retags-the-playground-document-schema/`, whose `(before, mutation, after, diff, outcome)` quintet pins exactly that wire shape and is already unit-tested inside the production crate (`committed_json_is_canonical`, `produces_committed_diff`, `committed_diff_applies_to_after`, `declared_outcome_holds`), plus the inverse law as a metamorphic property: retagging and then applying the mutation's own computed inverse must restore the committed before-document. The `mutate-playground-1` case re-exercises those SAME committed bytes end-to-end through `apply_playground_mutation`/`inverse_playground_mutation` rather than calling `Mutation::diff`/`inverse` directly the way the in-crate fixture test does.
